explanation: Tipping in Greek restaurants is voluntary rather than obligatory; locals typically round up the bill or leave a small amount in cash. At casual tavernas a couple of euros per person (roughly 5-10%) is typical, while upscale restaurants may see 10-15% for excellent service, well below American-style tipping norms.
local_tip: Leave a small cash tip (round up the bill or about 5-10%) directly on the table rather than adding it to a card payment.
regional_note: In touristy island towns and high-end Athens restaurants, tipping closer to 10-15% is more common, while in neighborhood tavernas rounding up is enough.

also_check.note: Tipping is considered unnecessary and can even cause confusion or offense; excellent service is the baseline norm.
Tipping 15-20% is standard and expected for good service, as servers rely on tips for income.
Service charge is included by law, but leaving small change for good service is still a nice, common gesture.
